clue.text: As a result, I made "part" the last syllable

indicators.note: the word part, set in quotation marks, says only a portion of the neighbouring words is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone explains a grammatical consequence, having labelled the final syllable of a word a 'part'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' tells you to take a run of letters from 'result, I made', reading across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody the ultima is the technical term for the final syllable of a word.

clue.text: A lot of sailors covering the state included in drinks for breakfast?

indicators.note: the sailors and the state are placed within the drinks

parts.note: Cokes are colas, soft drinks

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece covering another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is a large body of sailors
FLA is an abbreviation for the US state of Florida

explanation.surface: A big crew of sailors toasts a US state with drinks at the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' in a down clue means sitting on top. The question mark marks the definition as an example: the answer is a breakfast, not breakfast itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of this toasted maize cereal is a typical example of a morning meal.

clue.text: A line of sea mist showing in Derbyshire

parts.note: a fret is a sea mist rolling in off the North Sea coast of England
a film that is on is showing

explanation.surface: A band of coastal fog is visible somewhere in the Peak District county.
explanation.walkthrough: Derbyshire is an English county in the Midlands; FRET is a regional word for a sea fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfreton is a market town located in the county of Derbyshire, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Beat down crone with gammy leg

parts.note: a crone is an ugly old woman, a hag

indicators.note: a gammy leg is a lame or injured one, so the word is twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: An old woman with a bad leg is attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gammy' (British slang for lame) rearranges LEG into GLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat down a seller is to bargain hard over the price, the same act as haggling.

clue.text: Gee/horse? Anyway, we're off!

indicators.note: read as 'in any way', it says the letters before it may be arranged however you like

explanation.surface: A rider urges a horse on and announces the start of the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyway' rearranges the eight letters of GEE and HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Said at the start of a risky venture, the phrase is an exclamation of setting off.

clue.text: Denied benefits? Help!

parts.note: gains are benefits or profits
aid means help

explanation.surface: A claimant refused welfare payments cries out for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'benefits' suggests state welfare in the surface, but here it just means advantages.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so its past tense matches denied.

clue.text: Failure of wood holding everyone back

indicators.note: the wood holds the other piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: back says the word for everyone is read in reverse

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A forest fails while everyone retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALL into LLA, which COPSE holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a sudden breakdown or failure, as of a business or plan.

clue.text: Mine contains name of volume

indicators.note: the mine has the other letter inside it

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A colliery holds the name of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: A PINT is an imperial unit of liquid volume, just over half a litre in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a unit of liquid measure, an amount of volume.

clue.text: Jug you are said to provide

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: spoken quickly, these two words sound like a jug's name

explanation.surface: Someone is told they have to supply the pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed jug, traditionally for washing water.

clue.text: Fruit managed to protect one's ego

indicators.note: the managing word wraps round the others, shielding them

parts.note: to run something is to manage it, past tense ran
one is I, and the 's adds S
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in shielding their own self-esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives two letters, I and the S of the possessive; 'ego' is Latin for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Opening for transport

definitions.meaning: a way in, a door or gateway
as a verb, to transport is to enrapture, the sense of the verb stressed on its second syllable

explanation.surface: A gap or doorway for vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: EN-trance (a way in) and en-TRANCE (to delight).
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a doorway; the other, a verb, means to delight or carry away with emotion.

clue.text: Volga Street thus wildly depicted by composer

indicators.note: wildly says the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A Russian river's street scene is portrayed vividly by a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges VOLGA, ST and THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer wrote The Planets suite, so he is a classic example of a composer.

clue.text: Hot soubrette (a model manqué) could be somewhere around

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become something else when rearranged
manqué means failed or missing, so the model's letter is lost and the a stands in

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model can give T

explanation.surface: A hot young actress who failed as a model might be found nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: In SOUBRETTE one T (the Model T) is swapped for A, then 'could be' rearranges those letters with H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereabouts means in this general area, roughly near here.

clue.text: Beast heard it outside retreat in the west

indicators.note: heard says the beast's name is spoken, giving letters that sound like it

parts.note: an ox is a beast of burden

indicators.note: the two letters of it sit around the retreat

parts.note: taken as written
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A creature can be heard outside its hiding place out west.
explanation.walkthrough: OCC sounds like OX at the start of the answer; IT goes outside DEN to give IDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is a literary name for the western world, as opposed to the Orient.

clue.text: Childless fellow studied to appear brilliant

parts.note: SP stands for sine prole, Latin for without offspring, used in genealogies
Len is a man's name, standing for any fellow
to do a subject is to study it, so did means studied

explanation.surface: A man without children did his studies and shone.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole) is a genealogical abbreviation meaning died without issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid means magnificent or excellent, much like brilliant.

clue.text: He turns out at quarter to six? Blimey, about time!

indicators.note: quarter to six puts the quarter's letter just before the six

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass
VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about the letter for time

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise like blimey

explanation.surface: Someone checks the clock at a quarter to six and exclaims that it is about time.
explanation.walkthrough: COR and 'Blimey' are both British exclamations of surprise; COR goes about T to make CTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is someone who turns people out of a property, a cryptic way of saying he ejects.

clue.text: Did poor Ruth deny being sultry?

indicators.note: poor suggests the words are in bad shape and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ruth is asked whether she denied being seductive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges RUTH and DENY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundery weather is close and oppressive, which is what sultry means of the air.

clue.text: Bog plant to be presented as royal prize

parts.note: a king is a royal
a cup is a sporting prize

explanation.surface: A marsh plant is awarded as a trophy by a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingcup, or marsh marigold, is a yellow-flowered plant of wet bogs.

clue.text: Not positive, but it's acceptable for simple lock to be held back

parts.note: U, short for upper class, is used of something socially acceptable

indicators.note: the simple word holds the lock inside it

parts.note: naive means simple or unsophisticated

indicators.note: back says the word for a lock is read in reverse

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A diffident person accepts that a basic lock must be pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TRESS into SSERT, which NAIVE holds; U for acceptable is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Unassertive means lacking confidence, not forceful or positive in manner.

clue.text: Think about a boy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone ponders a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to think things through logically.

clue.text: Tot's taking mother across river

indicators.note: the mother stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A small child is carried over a river by its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler, but it is a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits, the same as a dram of whisky.

clue.text: Rising artist, ignoring society, matured

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top
ignoring says a letter is dropped

parts.note: Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming painter who shuns society has grown older.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGAS loses S ('ignoring') to give DEGA, and 'Rising' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means grown old or matured, as with wine or cheese.

clue.text: Dance turnout fuss continuing

parts.note: a rig is an outfit, one's turnout
ado means fuss
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: A ball's turnout has caused an ongoing commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The rigadoon is a lively Baroque dance for couples.

clue.text: Finish with a little outside knowledge

indicators.note: the small amount goes outside the knowledge

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
gen is British slang for information or knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone completes a task with a smattering of external expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag end is the last part or tail end of something, its finish.

clue.text: Friend coming out of the river will be reasonable

indicators.note: the friend's letters split and emerge on either side of the river

parts.note: a mate is a friend
the Oder is a river of central Europe

explanation.surface: A pal emerging from the water will be sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate means within reasonable limits, not extreme.

clue.text: Was entertainer diverted to shed?

indicators.note: diverted says the letters are sent off course and rearranged

explanation.surface: An entertainer was sent off to the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges TO and SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To host is to act as the entertainer of guests, so its past tense fits.
